title: Money matters
description: Pay, borrow and count what things cost.
grammar: the conditional for money problems, and the words of paying
grammarNote: The conditional says what would happen: pagaría todo, no me prestaría el dinero.

explanation.summary: Money has a vocabulary of its own: what you owe, what you save and what a thing costs. This unit gives you the nouns and the verbs for paying, borrowing and counting the cost.

sections.heading: Paying and counting
sections.body: Una factura is the bill you are given, and un recibo is the slip that proves you paid. El coste is what a thing costs in general, and la cuota is the part you pay each time: pago la cuota de la luz. Most of these nouns are feminine, except el coste and el recibo.

examples.es: Guarda el recibo, por si acaso.
examples.en: Keep the receipt, just in case.

examples.es: El coste de la vida sube cada año.
examples.en: The cost of living goes up every year.

sections.heading: Borrowing
sections.body: Un préstamo is money you borrow and give back, and una deuda is what you owe. El interés is what the loan costs you: el banco me cobra un interés alto. Devolver is to give back, and it is the verb you need when the money goes home.

examples.en: I asked the bank for a loan.

examples.es: Le devolví el dinero el lunes.
examples.en: I gave him the money back on Monday.

sections.heading: Spending and saving
sections.body: Gastar is to spend, and el ahorro is what you keep: ahorra una parte de cada mes. If you spend more than you earn, you say what you would do: no pagaría eso. Pagar takes a con when you say how you paid: pago con tarjeta.

examples.en: I spend too much on food.

examples.es: Mi ahorro está en el banco.
examples.en: My savings are at the bank.
I would never pay for that.

items.note: Masculine: el préstamo. It takes an accent on the e.
The verb devolver: devuelvo, devuelves, devuelve.
Masculine: el interés. It takes an accent on the e.
Feminine: la cuota. You pay it every month.
The verb gastar: gasto, gastas, gasta.

drills.prompt: La ___ dice cuánto tengo que pagar.
drills.meaning: the bill says how much I have to pay

drills.prompt: Pedí un ___ de dos mil euros.
drills.meaning: I asked for a loan of two thousand euros

drills.prompt: Pago una ___ de ochenta euros cada mes.
drills.meaning: I pay an instalment of eighty euros every month
I gave him the money back on Monday

drills.prompt: El ___ de la vida ha subido mucho.
drills.meaning: the cost of living has gone up a lot
